subject: grayWolf
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: gray wolf standing alert.
Style: Blizzard/Warcraft.
reasoning:
Looking at the renders, the mane tufts read as stiff flat spikes standing nearly vertical like porcupine quills instead of lying back naturally, so I need to adjust the extrude orientation and direction of the tuft helper to make them sweep backward.

The jaw also looks like a detached cream tube floating below the head loft rather than connecting smoothly — I should raise it slightly and tighten the overlap so it reads as part of the skull. Front legs are fine as straight pillars, and I notice the obelisk is getting visually swallowed by the overlapping wolf and pine shapes, which I'll need to address too.

Trying other spots near the obelisk still puts the pine too far out or colliding with the tail, so I'll settle on placing it closer in at roughly (-0.55,-0.95) and shrink the cone radius down to about 0.24 to avoid overhang.

Now I'm checking the obelisk box against the pine footprint—they don't overlap. But one of the rocks near (-0.4,-0.97) conflicts with the tail area, so I'm repositioning it to around (0.2,-1.05) instead. I'm also double-checking whether the pine would be visible or blocked in the left-side view.

Looking at the eyes next, they feel too small and the cyan war-paint dots read as noisy, so I'm bumping the eye radius from 0.075 to 0.09 and keeping the orange glow. Then I notice the banner pole visually crosses the wolf's collar/head line in the three-quarter view, so I'm shifting the banner to x=-1.0, z=0.7, checking the hypotenuse stays within radius, and considering reversing the arm direction so the banner extends toward +x instead of hanging oddly off the plinth edge.

Repositioning the banner toward +x fixes the collar overlap, but now it collides with the obelisk in front view, so I'm testing BX=0.9, BZ=0.6 with the arm reaching toward the wolf, landing the banner center around x=0.7 — clear of the wolf's body width and close enough to the crystals and pole without real conflict, while the obelisk stays put on the left.

Checking the three-quarter view next: the pole is thin edge-on from the side, so it shouldn't block the chest much, but I need to confirm camera placement — if it's looking from +x/+z, the banner there still intrudes on the face, so I'm trying moving it to the back instead, around BX=0.85, BZ=-0.55 where the pine used to sit, with the arm pointing toward -x near the wolf's hindquarters.

I'll angle the arm toward +x with the banner centered around -0.75,0.55, keeping clear of the wolf's paw positions near z 0.46. Settling on BX=-1.0, BZ=0.5 with the obelisk separated at z=-0.45, checking the pole length against that offset.

Now I'm adjusting the fur spikes, which is really the key fix: shortening the mane tufts, shrinking the upward vector and scaling length down, then reworking the side vectors so the blade orientation lies flat along the right plane using the cross product between the tuft direction and the surface normal.

Checking the cross product confirms the side vector points correctly, so the mane blades lie flat and tilted back about 7 degrees for a shingled look. I'm adjusting the embed depth and up vector so the blades lift slightly away from the surface, then moving on to the neck ring tufts where the up direction combines the outward offset with the reversed forward tangent.

I'll shorten the tuft lengths slightly, from 0.2 to 0.15 and 0.15 to 0.12, and leave the rest as is since the spiky black leaf shapes on the neck and body, plus the chin tuft and cheek ruff, all look fine. Checking the hips, body proportions, and tail tufts, everything reads correctly for this high-set quadruped pose, but I notice an odd thin white vertical line above the head in the front view that I can't quite place—possibly a stray spike or artifact I need to investigate further.

That floating pendant spike below the banner needs adjusting since it's slightly detached from the banner plane—I'll reposition it to sit flush at the bottom edge, and I'll leave the octahedron crystal above the obelisk alone since that's intentional. I'm also nudging the jaw sweep points and fang position upward slightly for a tighter fit, then moving on to adjusting eye size and writing out the precise edits.

Adjusting mane tuft code...

I'm reworking the pine tree parameters (PX, PZ, radius taper) and the rock placement coordinates near the tail, then preparing a contiguous replacement for the banner block covering BX through the pendant lines.
